title: Local prefilter cache for tail-based trace sampling to reduce agent CPU and RPC overhead
creator: Asha Patel
description: Reduce CPU and network overhead from tail-based trace sampling in the agent by introducing a lightweight local prefilter cache that avoids calling the central sampler for common service/pattern combinations. This reduces RPCs, improves tail latencies, and prevents sampling-induced perf regressions for high-throughput paths.
acceptance_criteria: Agent CPU consumption from tracing hooks reduced by >=30% in 95th percentile hosts under baseline traffic in lab
Number of sampler RPCs from agent to central sampler reduced by >=50% for top-10 services in staging
No increase in request p95 latency above 2% compared to baseline (observed across 3 representative workloads), and no external error rate increase
Unit + integration tests for cache correctness and eviction behavior added to tracing-agent test suite
Feature flag + phased rollout documented and dashboarded for monitoring metrics and easy rollback
tasks: Design cache key: (service, route_hash, environment) with TTL and LFU prefilter eviction
Add a light-weight in-memory prefilter inside the agent to answer 'should_sample' for common keys
Implement async background refresh path for cache misses to avoid blocking request threads
Benchmark prototype in lab against trace-heavy workload generator (100k reqs/s), record CPU, RPC, and latency
Address concurrency: replace coarse mutex with per-shard lock-free queue to avoid contention on hot keys
Add feature flag and config knobs (cache_ttl_ms, cache_size, prefilter_threshold) exposed via agent config
Create staging rollout plan (10% -> 30% -> 60% -> 100%) with automated health checks
Create dashboards and alerts: agent_sampling_rpc_rate, agent_sampling_cache_hit_rate, agent_cpu_core_seconds, request_p95_latency, trace_drop_rate
PR + code review, merge, and canary rollout
comments: 2026-02-25 - Asha Patel: Triage note — multiple customers and internal SLOs hit by tracing-induced CPU spikes. Proposed local prefilter cache as lowest-risk mitigation compared to full adaptive sampling redesign.

2026-03-01 - Diego Morales: Prototype completed. Simple map+TTL reduces sampler RPCs by ~58% on the top-10 services in lab. However observed mutex contention on a hotspot route causing occasional request latency spikes.
2026-03-03 - Sofia Chen (review): Requested change — avoid blocking fast-path: add async refresh and return cached false for misses when under cpu pressure. Added to tasks.

2026-03-06 - Diego Morales: Implemented sharded ring buffer and per-shard atomic counters. Local bench shows CPU 38% lower p95 compared to baseline and RPC rate down 63%. p95 request latency unchanged in 3/3 workloads; one workload had +1.6% which is within acceptance criteria.

2026-03-09 - Marcus Li (perf): Noted a regression in cold-start behavior where initial cache warmup causes burst of RPCs. Plan: seed cache on startup with most recent policy snapshot and add jittered prefetch.
2026-03-11 - Diego Morales: Submitted PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/agent/pull/4521 — includes code, unit tests, and benchmark harness. Requesting review from Sofia, Marcus, and QA.
2026-03-12 - QA (Elena Novak): Ran staging smoke tests with canary config. Observed stable behavior for 48h at 20% traffic. Added integration test to assert cache hit rate >40% for target services.

2026-03-13 - Diego Morales: Updated rollout playbook, created dashboard tile: agent_sampling_cache_hit_rate and alert: sampling_cache_hit_rate < 20% for 10m. Ready for limited canary (10% prod) pending approvals.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Cold-start burst of sampler RPCs. Mitigation: seed cache from last snapshot and staggered prefetch on startup.

Risk: Cache correctness could cause unintended sampling bias. Mitigation: keep cache TTL small (configurable), audit logs for decisions, and maintain fast path to query central sampler for low-confidence keys.
Risk: Lock contention on hot keys. Mitigation: sharded atomic structures and lock-free ring for updates; benchmarked under synthetic hotspots.
Risk: Unexpected interaction with adaptive sampling in central controller. Mitigation: add compatibility tests and ensure central sampler ignores prefilter cache responses for rollout windows.
deployment_plan: Stage 1 (canary): Enable feature flag for 10% of agent fleet in us-west for 72h, monitor CPU and cache hit rate
Stage 2: If stable, expand to 30% across additional regions for 72h and validate p95 latency and sampler RPC reduction
Stage 3: 60% -> 100% with 48h observation windows and automated rollback on defined alerts
Rollback: Feature flag off triggers agents to remove cache and resume previous sampling behavior immediately
monitoring_playbook: Watch: agent_cpu_core_seconds — alert if host CPU increase >10% vs baseline after rollout
Watch: agent_sampling_rpc_rate — decreased trend expected; alert if increases by >15% vs baseline
Watch: request_p95_latency & error_rate — immediate rollback on >2% latency regression or any error rate regression >0.5%
Create runbook steps for on-call to roll back flag and gather trace dump for postmortem
notes: We intentionally avoid full adaptive tail-sampling changes in this ticket to keep risk low and implement an incremental optimization that buys runway for a larger redesign later.
Trade-off: Slight staleness in sampling decisions (TTL) vs. large CPU/RPC savings. TTL is configurable per-customer for high-compliance customers.
Benchmarks (lab): baseline agent host CPU p95: 2.8 cores, with prefilter: 1.7 cores; sampler RPCs/s (top services) baseline: 1500 -> 540 after prefilter (63% reduction).
